findings.title: Masking randomness reuse is not detected in synthesized hardware
findings.location: Masking PRNG update path (`prd_masking_upd`, `prd_sub_bytes_q`) and assertions `AesSecCmKeyMaskingPrdSubBytes` / `AesSecCmKeyMaskingInitialPrngUpdate*`
findings.description: When `SecMasking` is enabled, the security of SubBytes and key expansion depends on advancing the masking PRNG between nonlinear evaluations. The controller drives the single-rail `prd_masking_upd` signal without an update acknowledgment, freshness counter, or runtime error check. A precisely timed clock/voltage/EM fault that suppresses an asserted update can therefore leave `prd_masking`, `prd_sub_bytes_q`, and `prd_key_expand` unchanged for a subsequent evaluation. This condition is not included in `mux_sel_err` or `sp_enc_err_d` and consequently does not raise `alert_o` or force the controller into its terminal error state. Freshness is checked only by SVAs under `INC_ASSERT`, which are not synthesized. Reusing randomness across masked nonlinear evaluations violates the masking scheme's fresh-randomness assumption and can enable correlation or probing-assisted key recovery over repeated attacker-triggered operations.
findings.recommendation: Add a synthesized, fault-resistant PRNG update protocol. For example, have `aes_prng_masking` return a sparsely encoded update acknowledgment or freshness epoch and require the controller to verify that it advances before enabling SubBytes or key expansion. Latch any mismatch as a fatal error, inhibit `out_valid_o`, and securely clear state and key registers. Protect the update request and freshness state with sparse or redundant encoding rather than relying solely on the existing non-synthesized assertions.
